title: The shadow that slowed production
blurb: The draft ran shadows inline with no deadline and no isolation.
prompt: Production latency doubled during a semblance run because the draft called the candidate inline on the request thread with no deadline, and shadow traffic consumed tenants production rate limits. The same report declared a winner from twelve samples. Review it, fix it, and prove shadows cannot reach production in any way.
aiNote: The draft makes the candidate call synchronously inside the production handler with no deadline and shares the tenant's production rate-limit buckets and idempotency store, so an unhealthy candidate both slows and starves the real path.
testIdea: Stub the candidate to hang and assert production p99 is unchanged; exhaust the shadow budget and assert production quota is untouched; feed 12 pairs and assert the report says inconclusive.
followUps: What metrics can a shadow observably improve before deployment?
How would you compare cost between candidate and production paths?
When is a 5 percent share too much?
